subject: Game Theory
title: What Is a Social Dilemma?
description: A short lesson to help you apply What Is a Social Dilemma?.

hook.text: Every commuter prefers driving. If everyone drives, traffic is gridlocked. The bus would've been faster for all.

buildup.text: A social dilemma: individual rationality produces collective irrationality. What's best for me hurts us all.

discovery.text: The structure is always the same: a dominant strategy for each player leads to a dominated outcome for the group.

twist.text: Social dilemmas aren't failures of morality—they're failures of structure. Smart people make bad outcomes inevitable.

climax.text: Climate change, overfishing, arms races, and antibiotic overuse are all social dilemmas hiding in plain sight.

punchline.text: When everyone optimizes alone, everyone loses.

quiz.question: What defines a social dilemma?
options: Individual rationality leads to collectively worse outcomes
